open_points.subject: service-token disclosure ceiling
open_points.text: A09 uses “the highest disclosure class”, “a class above”, and `class(answer(op)) <= highest_class(s)`, but no text orders `open`, `business_confidential` and `personal_data`.
open_points.question: What is the ordering of the three disclosure classes used to decide whether an answer exceeds a token's ceiling?
options: `open < business_confidential < personal_data`
Classes are incomparable capabilities and each allowed class must be listed explicitly
open_points.default_guess: Use `open < business_confidential < personal_data`.

open_points.subject: create replay after erasure
open_points.text: A01 rule 8 says “a create arriving after that with the same request id is a new create”, while R0-36 says a create repeated after a lost answer “never silently makes a second project, customer or room”.
open_points.question: After anonymisation or customer erasure removes the stored request id, must a delayed retry remain deduplicated or may it create a second record?
options: Keep enough replay information to prevent a second create
Treat the request id as forgotten and allow a new create
open_points.default_guess: Keep a non-personal replay tombstone so the retry cannot create a second record.

open_points.subject: checks performed before create replay
open_points.text: A01 rule 3 says “No other precondition of the create is checked again for a repeat”, but A04 rule 6 says “Only an action that passes all six may be a repeat”.
open_points.question: For a request-id replay, which current validations besides caller rights, session access and project archival are rerun before the stored record is returned?
options: Only the checks expressly named by A01 rule 3
Every applicable A04 check
A separate per-create list of replay checks
open_points.default_guess: Apply A01's specific replay rule: check current authority and the expressly named archival condition, then compare replay facts.

open_points.subject: confirmation validation in the common check order
open_points.text: A04 declares one first-failure order for every action, while A13 adds session-bound CSRF and one-time confirmation values without placing either check in that order.
open_points.question: At what point are CSRF and confirmation values checked, and which refusal wins when authentication, rights, target existence, revision, lifecycle or confirmation also fails?
options: Check session, CSRF and confirmation before all record checks
Check confirmation after target and revision checks
Define a complete order separately for confirmed owner actions
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate the owner session, check CSRF, then validate and consume confirmation before exposing any target-specific failure.

open_points.subject: withdrawal project selection
open_points.text: A10 rule 2 says an operation on a project that names none uses the session's active project, while A08 rule 7 says “A withdrawal names the pointer only; its project is the pointer's own”.
open_points.question: When Kernel withdraws a pointer and the session's active project differs from the pointer's project, is authorization checked against the pointer's project or the active project?
options: Always use the pointer's own project
Require or infer the active project and require it to match
Require an explicit project id as well as the pointer id
open_points.default_guess: Resolve the pointer first without disclosing it, then authorize against the pointer's own project.

open_points.subject: session identity reused after ending
open_points.text: A11 says “Registering the same identity again makes a new session”, while M06 treats the session identity as the entity's continuing identity and M09 audit subjects contain only that identity.
open_points.question: How are the old and new session incarnations distinguished in audit entries and other references when Kernel reuses the same session identity?
options: Forbid reuse of an ended session identity
Add an incarnation or registration identity
Accept that audit entries for separate sessions are indistinguishable
open_points.default_guess: Forbid reuse and require Kernel to supply a new session identity.

open_points.subject: access version when a session ends
open_points.text: A12 rule 1 says every accepted action changing the granted set, active project or pending request moves the version, rule 3 includes ending among version-checked owner actions, but A11 says ending removes the record and its access version.
open_points.question: Does ending a session conceptually increment its access version before deletion, or is ending exempt from the version-movement rule while still requiring the stated current version?
options: Check the version but delete without incrementing it
Increment and retain a terminal version somewhere
Do not require a version for ending
open_points.default_guess: Require the current version as a concurrency check, then delete without an observable increment.

open_points.subject: OwnerSession facts needed by the access rules
open_points.text: M11 says the OwnerSession facts are its identity, began instant and written-once expiry, while A13 requires mutable last-request time, CSRF state and one-time confirmation values “kept in the owner session”. State 1 says the listed facts are all facts.
open_points.question: Are last activity, CSRF state and pending confirmation values facts of OwnerSession, derived values, or separate runtime records, and can the session's expiry change?
options: Extend OwnerSession with mutable runtime facts
Keep a fixed absolute expiry and store idle/CSRF/confirmation state separately
Derive all of them without stored state
open_points.default_guess: Extend the temporary OwnerSession state with last activity, CSRF material and pending confirmations while keeping the eight-hour expiry fixed.

open_points.subject: failed-sign-in counter
open_points.text: A13 counts “the refused sign-ins of the last 15 minutes” but does not say whether malformed or missing-credential submissions count, or whether a refusal exactly 15 minutes old remains in the window.
open_points.question: Which refused sign-in requests count toward lockout, and are window and lockout endpoints inclusive or exclusive?
options: Count every syntactically valid attempt with an incorrect credential; use half-open time intervals
Count every sign-in refusal except those during lockout
Count only completed credential comparisons that fail
open_points.default_guess: Count every non-lockout sign-in request that reaches credential verification and fails; exclude events whose age is at least 15 minutes.

open_points.subject: confirmation-value consumption
open_points.text: A13 says a confirmation value “is used up by the first submission, whatever its answer” but also that it is valid only in its session and every change requires valid CSRF protection.
open_points.question: Does a submission with a missing or wrong owner session, invalid CSRF value, malformed request, or mismatched action consume an otherwise valid confirmation value?
options: Consume only after session, CSRF and binding checks pass
Consume whenever the value is presented, even from an invalid request
Specify different consumption rules for authentication failures and action refusals
open_points.default_guess: Consume atomically only after the owner session, CSRF and confirmation binding have been validated, but before domain checks.

open_points.subject: publish replay after artifact-type removal
open_points.text: A01 says no create precondition other than current rights and project archival is rechecked for a repeat, while A22 says after removal “publishing that type ... [is] refused as an unknown type”.
open_points.question: Does a replay of an earlier publish request id return its existing pointer after the type has been removed, or is it refused as an unknown type?
options: Return the existing pointer because it is a replay
Refuse because the type is no longer declared
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing pointer after the current authority checks, because no new pointer or version is being published.

open_points.subject: data shown in the import mapping
open_points.text: A16 says the mapping shows each project “with its id, status, rooms and pointers” and the replacement name and alias, but the accepted import also stores its object, customer link, source instants and other project facts; the consequence says the owner sees “exactly what will arrive”.
open_points.question: Which imported facts must be displayed for owner review before confirmation, especially object personal data, customer links, source timestamps and pointer details?
options: Show every fact that the accepted transaction will store
Show only the fields expressly listed in A16
Show summaries for some facts and full values on demand
open_points.default_guess: Show every stored fact or an unambiguous full representation of it before confirmation.

open_points.subject: lifetime of an uploaded import file
open_points.text: A16 says upload changes nothing, confirmation later applies “the file of that digest”, and a test confirms an earlier mapping after another file was uploaded, but no rule says where uploaded bytes are kept, whether they must be uploaded again, or when they are discarded.
open_points.question: How does Registry obtain the exact file at confirmation, and when are unconfirmed, expired, consumed or superseded uploads removed?
options: Keep session-scoped temporary uploads until confirmation expiry or use
Require the file to be uploaded again and verify its digest
Keep a global digest-addressed upload cache
open_points.default_guess: Keep the upload as session-scoped temporary data and remove it on use, confirmation expiry, session end or restart.

open_points.subject: withdrawn pointers in migration files
open_points.text: M05 says an imported pointer “is never imported `withdrawn`”, while A16 treats a pointer as malformed only when its status is outside the vocabulary, whose vocabulary includes `withdrawn`.
open_points.question: Must a picked project containing a `withdrawn` pointer be refused, or may that status be imported?
options: Refuse every imported `withdrawn` pointer
Allow it and define its withdrawal instant and principal
Normalize it to another status
open_points.default_guess: Refuse it, matching M05's explicit import rule.

open_points.subject: validity of imported pointer histories and timestamps
open_points.text: A16 checks versions `1..n`, at most one `published` pointer and readable instants, but says nothing about lifecycle-consistent status order, required transition instants, chronological ordering, or impossible project and pointer dates.
open_points.question: Which cross-record and chronological invariants must an import satisfy beyond the listed syntax checks?
options: Require every imported record to satisfy all M01–M05 lifecycle and time invariants
Accept any arrangement passing A16's explicit checks
Declare a separate exhaustive import-validity profile
open_points.default_guess: Require all domain lifecycle and chronology invariants, with an explicit exhaustive validation profile.

open_points.subject: digest used to bind an import
open_points.text: A16 and M10 identify the uploaded file only “by its digest”, without declaring the digest algorithm, encoding or whether two equal digests are treated as the same file.
open_points.question: Which collision-resistant digest and canonical representation bind the reviewed file to confirmation and the migration closure?
options: Declare a fixed algorithm and encoding in State 2
Defer the concrete algorithm and encoding to the States 5–6 contract
Use the raw file bytes with a release-selected algorithm
open_points.default_guess: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with SHA-256 and encode the result as lowercase hexadecimal.

open_points.subject: backup-location startup checks
open_points.text: A17 requires every configuration check to pass before serving and explicitly requires the store to open for reading and writing, but gives no corresponding accessibility or writability check for the configured backup location.
open_points.question: Must startup verify that the backup location exists, is writable and can safely create and delete backup files, or may Registry start and discover failure at 03:00?
options: Verify backup-location access at startup
Defer all backup-location checks to each backup run
Perform only non-mutating startup validation
open_points.default_guess: Perform a safe write-and-remove probe at startup and refuse to serve if it fails.

open_points.subject: restore-test authentication configuration
open_points.text: A18 requires the restored temporary instance to be “configured with no service token” and to start under A17, while A17 says configuration must contain one token for every A09 service and that a missing token stops startup.
open_points.question: How can the restore-test instance pass A17 without exposing service access?
options: Configure valid isolated tokens that no service possesses
Add an explicit restore-test configuration mode with no tokens
Test the store without starting Registry
open_points.default_guess: Configure fresh temporary tokens known only to the restore process and expose no network listener.

open_points.subject: production data in the restore-test instance
open_points.text: A18 calls the restored copy “a production instance for the test only” holding production data, while State 0 says there is one authoritative production instance and every other instance is a test instance that holds no production personal data.
open_points.question: What trust category and identity status does the temporary restored copy have, and is it an explicit exception to the one-production-instance and no-production-data-in-tests rules?
options: Define an isolated non-serving production restore environment as an explicit exception
Run the restore test only while the real production instance is stopped
Do not restore production data; test with synthetic data
open_points.default_guess: Define a short-lived, isolated restore environment inside VM Platform as an explicit exception, never reachable by services or agents.

open_points.subject: backup retention after failed runs
open_points.text: A18 deletes backups older than 30 days only “After a backup is written”, but a failed backup waits until the next 03:00 while Registry keeps serving; its formal invariants say no erased value remains after 30 days and the oldest backup is at most 30 days old after each run.
open_points.question: Must expiry deletion run even when creating the new backup fails, and what happens when deletion itself fails?
options: Run retention cleanup independently on every scheduled run
Retain old backups until a new successful backup exists
Stop serving when retention cleanup cannot meet the deadline
open_points.default_guess: Run cleanup independently after every scheduled attempt, report deletion failures prominently, and do not claim the 30-day bound unless cleanup succeeds.

open_points.subject: backup encryption format
open_points.text: A18 says each backup is “encrypted with the backup key” but does not declare an authenticated-encryption scheme, nonce handling, file format, integrity verification or key derivation.
open_points.question: What exact encryption and integrity rules make a backup confidential, tamper-evident and restorable across releases?
options: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope now
Leave the cryptographic format to implementation
Use an external encrypted-volume or backup tool format
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope with a fresh random nonce and explicit algorithm metadata.

open_points.subject: backup-key rotation
open_points.text: A17 allows configuration changes at the next start and holds exactly one backup key; A18 does not say what happens to backups encrypted under the previous key.
open_points.question: When the backup key changes, are existing backups re-encrypted, retained with old keys, or deleted and replaced?
options: Re-encrypt all retained backups atomically
Keep a versioned key ring for the retention period
Delete old-key backups after first successful new-key backup
open_points.default_guess: Keep a versioned key ring until every backup encrypted with an old key has expired.

open_points.subject: release restore test versus store version
open_points.text: A18 says before each release the latest backup is restored and the instance must start under A17, while A17 refuses a store whose version differs from the running release and says migration is a separate release step.
open_points.question: Is the restore test run with the old release, the candidate release after applying its store migration, or both?
options: Restore and start with the old release only
Restore, migrate, and start with the candidate release
Test both pre-migration restore and candidate-release migration
open_points.default_guess: Test both: verify restoration with the source release, then apply the release migration and start the candidate release.

open_points.subject: reapplying erasures before restored production serves
open_points.text: A18 says erasures after the backup are repeated “before the instance serves again”, but the only defined erasure actions are made through the authenticated owner interface, which cannot be used if Registry serves nothing.
open_points.question: Through what defined mode or operation does the owner replay erasures before normal service is enabled?
options: Start an owner-only maintenance mode
Apply an offline restore journal before startup
Temporarily serve the owner interface while withholding the service API
open_points.default_guess: Start a maintenance mode exposing only the owner interface over the owner's protected path, with all service and agent access disabled.

open_points.subject: claimed one-day recovery point
open_points.text: A18 allows any number of daily backup failures while Registry keeps serving, but its consequence says data survives store loss “with at most a day of changes lost”.
open_points.question: Is the one-day recovery-point objective guaranteed, or is it conditional on the latest scheduled backup succeeding?
options: Make serving contingent on having a successful backup within 24 hours
State that the one-day loss bound is conditional, not guaranteed
Add retries and escalation sufficient to preserve a hard bound
open_points.default_guess: State the bound as conditional on a successful backup within the preceding 24 hours.

open_points.subject: verification of encrypted-disk and VM isolation invariants
open_points.text: A18 requires the store and backups to be on encrypted VM Platform disks and unreachable from VM Agent, but defines no startup, release or required test that verifies either property.
open_points.question: What evidence or automated check establishes disk encryption and VM Agent isolation before the backup and at-rest guarantees are claimed?
options: Add release/deployment checks with recorded evidence
Treat both solely as owner-attested deployment assumptions
Have Registry refuse startup unless it can verify them
open_points.default_guess: Make them explicit deployment prerequisites verified by release checks and recorded evidence outside Registry.

open_points.subject: completeness of the security review
open_points.text: A21 says “Every security category has exactly one outcome below”, but no text defines the complete set of security categories against which the listed categories can be checked.
open_points.question: What authoritative category or threat-model catalogue determines that the review is complete rather than merely complete for the categories someone happened to list?
options: Declare an exhaustive category catalogue in the specification
Reference a named, versioned external review standard
Limit the claim to the categories explicitly listed
open_points.default_guess: Limit the invariant to the explicitly enumerated categories unless a versioned catalogue is declared.
